title: McMullin Steamer Inn, lower Main Street, burned 1933
description: The historic McMullin Homestead on lower Main Street was lost to fire on February 11, 1933, leaving three families without a home. Only two chimneys, each with seven fireplaces once used for cooking, survived the blaze. Built in 1830 by Rev. Charles McMullin, who married Lawrence Wilsey’s daughter, the homestead was one of the area’s oldest and most storied buildings. Over the years, it served as a hotel, tavern, and steamer stop for travellers on the Saint John River. The fire was discovered by W. P. McMullin, who quickly alerted his family, but despite help from neighbors and the fire department, the house could not be saved. Residents, Mr. and Mrs. W. P. McMullin, Mr. and Mrs. Claude McMullin, and Mr. and Mrs. Milo McMullin, lost both their home and many treasured family heirlooms. Known for its solid construction and long history in the McMullin family, the homestead’s loss marked the end of an era for this region of New Brunswick.
